Six blocks. A prints a string to stdout, which is the path `qd` takes today. B and C hand the display machinery a real GT object. D and E hand it a shim advertising a chosen mimebundle, to establish what the consumer would do if `text/plain` were on offer. F dumps the `QUARTO_*` environment, which is the only channel Quarto has for telling the kernel what it is rendering.

```{python}
from fixture import table, Bundle
from IPython.display import display
```

## A. print path: a string on stdout

```{python}
print(table('A print').text)
```

## B. display path: bare expression

```{python}
table('B expr')
```

## C. display path: explicit display()

```{python}
display(table('C display'))
```

## D. shim: text/plain only

```{python}
display(Bundle('D plain', ['text/plain']))
```

## E. shim: text/html plus text/plain

```{python}
display(Bundle('E both', ['text/html', 'text/plain']))
```

## F. what Quarto tells the kernel

```{python}
import os
print({k: v for k, v in sorted(os.environ.items()) if k.startswith('QUARTO')})
```
